Subject: Consolidating maintenance windows + credit cap ask

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for the latest order form. Our legal and ops teams reviewed the SLA exhibit and we have two asks before we can move to internal procurement:

1) Maintenance windows — can Redwood consolidate planned maintenance into one monthly 4-hour window (rather than multiple monthly windows) and provide at least 72 hours notice for planned maintenance? We need predictability for our nightly ETL jobs.

2) Credit cap — your current draft leaves credits uncapped for sustained incidents. We typically accept a cap of no more than 3 months of recurring fees for an incident. Would Redwood accept a hard cap (or a proportional cap tied to the term)?

We attached a redline of the order form (Evergreen_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf) and an example credits matrix for reference (SLA_Credit_Ladder_v2.xlsx). Happy to hop on a 30m call if that's easier.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — we're aiming to finalize the PO by next week.

Best,
Daniel

Subject: Re: Consolidating maintenance windows + credit cap ask

Daniel — thanks for the clear asks and the attachments. Quick responses below and proposed trade-offs:

1) Maintenance windows: We can consolidate to one scheduled maintenance window per month (up to 4 hours) for most customers on Dedicated/Hosted plans, with a standard 72-hour notice for planned maintenance that affects infrastructure-level interrupts. We would still need to reserve the right for "emergency maintenance" (security fixes, critical patches) with as much notice as possible; those would be excluded from credits. We will add explicit language to the exhibit to define "emergency maintenance."

2) Credit cap: Redwood's standard position is to avoid hard caps so customers are fully compensated for large outages. That said, to move the deal forward we can offer a compromise: cap credits at 6 months of monthly recurring charges per incident (or the prorated portion of MRC tied to the impacted service), instead of unlimited credits. We believe 6 months balances risk while allowing us to avoid unlimited exposure.

3) Response times: While your note didn't call these out specifically, our redline adjusts response SLAs. Proposed: P1 (system down) — 1 hour response, 4 hour remediation target; P2 — 4 hour response, 24 hour remediation target. We will surface the definitions in the exhibit.

If that sounds workable, I'll route a revised redline from Legal for final review (neha copied). If you'd like to discuss nuances around credit calculation (daily vs monthly, blended vs per-tenant), let's schedule a short call.

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Sales Operations — Redwood Inference

Subject: Redwood redline: SLA exhibit (maintenance + credit cap language)

Hi Daniel / Evergreen Contracts —

Attached is Redwood's redline to the SLA exhibit reflecting the positions Vivek outlined. Key clauses we've added:

- Planned Maintenance: defined as "scheduled maintenance announced at least 72 hours in advance". One consolidated monthly maintenance window up to 4 hours. We explicitly exclude planned maintenance from uptime calculations.

- Emergency Maintenance: defined with examples (critical security patching, urgent data integrity fixes). We will notify as soon as possible; emergency maintenance is excluded from credits.

- Credit Cap: we propose a per-incident cap equal to six (6) months of the monthly recurring charges attributable to the affected service. Calculation examples are included in the attached SLA_Credit_Ladder_v2.xlsx.

- Credit Calculation: credits will be calculated against the monthly service fee on a per-incident basis and paid as a one-time credit to the invoice following the incident, not as recurring refunds.

- Response/Remediation: P1/P2 definitions and response targets as below. We also added an escalation path and mandated post-incident RCA for P1 incidents.

Please review and indicate any non-starter items. If Evergreen requires a lower cap (e.g., 3 months), provide a short rationale so we can escalate to Finance and Legal for consideration.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Contracts — Redwood Inference

- Finance agrees 6 months is acceptable for this deal size (EVR expected ARR tier) as long as we lock minimums and exclude third-party pass-through costs. They prefer 4 months for larger enterprise deals, but for speed-to-close they'll accept 6.

Suggest we call out "maintenance window occurs on the second Tuesday of each month, 02:00-06:00 UTC (subject to change with 30 days' notice)" and provide the ability to shift the day with mutual consent.

Recommend we propose the 6-month cap and the exact maintenance cadence as above. Happy to draft final language for attachments.
